summary:
1.0.0 is the first stable version of Cellar. It changes little after 0.12.0, and upgrading needs no manual action.

Text in the theme colour is now readable in every theme. In light mode, the green, orange and yellow themes write it in a darker shade of their colour, and the red and rose themes, in both modes, in a slightly adjusted one, so that it stays readable on a highlighted row. This covers the number of selected bottles in the bottle details, the "Add … as a new item" entry of searchable lists, the barcodes that the barcode search finds, and wine names and a wine's website link under the pointer. Buttons and icons keep their colour.

For contributors: the interface components are now grouped by domain under `src/lib/components/` (wines, bottles, storage, barcode, statistics, forms, layout…), and `ui/` keeps only the shadcn-svelte primitives. Nothing changes for users.

Pressing Tab on a choice list, such as the delimiter of the CSV export and import, no longer changes its value: it only moves to the next field, and typing a letter still chooses an option. Since 0.12.0, tabbing past the delimiter set it to "Tab", so the export wrote tab-separated files and the import rejected every row. A CSV export made since then may be tab-separated: import it with "Tab" as the delimiter.

Backup downloads in Admin › Backups are more reliable. After a restore, a JSON import or a wipe, if the server refuses the download of the backup of the previous data or cannot be reached, an error now says so and tells you that the backup stays in the list of backups, where you can download it, instead of a message saying that your browser downloads it. "Download" in the list of backups no longer loads the file into the browser's memory: the browser saves it straight to the disk, even a backup of several hundred megabytes.

Cellar can no longer be shown inside a frame of another web site, such as a page of another app on the same NAS that could hide it under a decoy to make you click its buttons. A dashboard that showed Cellar inside a frame now shows an empty frame: open Cellar with a link instead.

Notes and wine descriptions now count their 5,000 characters the same way in the forms, the API and the imports: an emoji counts as two, as it already did in the forms. The API used to accept a longer note full of emoji that the app then refused to save again, and that a CSV export and import cut without saying so; a note the API accepts now comes back whole from a CSV export and import. Renaming a country, region, appellation, wine type, colour, classification, format or origin to a name that another entry already has in a different case, such as `FRANCE` when `France` exists, is now refused with a 409 error instead of creating a near-duplicate, as adding one already finds the existing entry. An entry can still change the case of its own name. Scripts that rename these entries through the API may now get this 409.

A few small fixes to the interface. In the bottle details, "Change location" and "Change bottle availability" now stay inside the dialog on a phone, instead of past its right edge, and stay in view while the list of bottles scrolls. The number field of the "Bottle count" filter of the wine list now has a name for screen readers. Texts that trail off, such as "Updating…" or "Search wines…", now end with a true ellipsis in English and in French, and long names under the bars of the statistics end with "…": pointing at one still shows the whole name. The container dialog now says why its save button is greyed while the name is empty.

On a phone, the long dialogs of the admin no longer run off the screen: "Export to CSV Files", "Import Images from ZIP", "Automatic Backup Settings" with an external cron job, "Barcode Settings", and deleting images that many wines use. In these dialogs and the other long ones of the admin, the title and the buttons stay in view while the content scrolls, and an error, such as exporting with no table chosen, shows just above the buttons. In the CSV import guide, the example file names are easier to read in every theme, and the list of tables, like the lists of the CSV and ZIP import reports, can be scrolled with the keyboard.

The dependencies take the fixes published up to 23 October, including DOMPurify 3.4.17 for three security advisories. The PDF library lists DOMPurify, but Cellar never loads it and the Docker image does not contain it.

0.12.0 finishes the clean-up that the audit before 1.0 asked for: theme colours, accessibility, the default reference lists, documentation and dependencies. Upgrading needs no manual action.

The default reference lists are more forgiving of edited files. A line whose name is blank, such as a line of spaces left in a file of your `csv-imports` folder, is now skipped and named in the logs, instead of adding a type, country, region or appellation without a name. `appellations.csv` is now UTF-8, and a copy saved as UTF-8 no longer gives names like "CÃ´tes"; copies saved as Latin-1 by earlier versions or by a spreadsheet still read correctly, and an unedited copy of the old file in `csv-imports` is replaced by the UTF-8 one at the next start. When a database migration fails at startup, the message now names the migrations that were pending. Importing a JSON export still refuses a row that lacks its id or its dates.

The Docker image now runs on Node 24.22.1, which Node.js published as a security release, and the dependencies take the fixes published up to 21 October. Pages and the API now send `Vary: Cookie, Accept-Language`, so a cache in front of Cellar, such as a reverse proxy, no longer serves a page in the language of another visitor; wine images do not, so that the browser keeps them after a login or a change of language. The browser no longer writes errors to its console; the messages shown on the page do not change. For contributors: lint refuses `console` outside server code and turns the rules that only warned into errors, `pnpm check` also checks `scripts/` and `drizzle.config.ts`, and `pnpm check:watch` recompiles the messages.

Documentation: the command that resets a forgotten access code now finds the database that `DATABASE_PATH` or `DATA_DIR` moves, and README-Docker.md says to mount the database's folder, not the file alone or a symbolic link, with which a restore fails or leaves the old data in place, and to keep that folder off a network share. It also says that a script that sends no `Origin` header gets a plain-text 403 unless it sends `Content-Type: application/json`, and that uploads need `Origin`. The log's warning about a missing `ORIGIN` now gives the host port in its example (`http://192.168.1.20:3005`). `docker-setup.sh` is removed: the Quick start of README-Docker.md gives the same steps. For contributors: the lists of what CI checks are complete, and the built server started without Docker needs `BODY_SIZE_LIMIT=512M` to restore a backup, import a ZIP or upload an image over 512 KB.

In dark mode, select lists, the date picker and scrollbars are now dark too. In light mode, the buttons of the green, orange and yellow themes now have dark text, which is easier to read on their pale colour. In dark mode, error messages and delete buttons use a lighter red, and the number of wines in shortage, in the menu, is on a darker red in both modes. The borders of form fields are darker in light mode and lighter in dark mode, so the fields stand out; in dark mode, the inside of fields, checkboxes and outlined buttons is a little lighter too. Switching from dark to light mode no longer leaves secondary buttons and the current menu entry with pale text on a pale background until the next reload.

Logged in, the first page you open already shows the Admin and Barcode links, the Logout button and the edit buttons, instead of Login until the page had loaded. Searchable lists, such as a wine's appellation or a bottle's wine, now work with the keyboard alone: the arrow keys move through the choices, Enter picks one and Escape closes the list, and a screen reader announces the list and the current choice. When a save is refused, the form scrolls to the first field in error and puts the cursor in it, on a phone too, and a screen reader reads the field's message with it. Each page now has its own title, so browser tabs and the history tell them apart. On the Preferences page, a screen reader announces each choice as a radio button and says which one is on, and the arrow keys move between them; the rows at the bottom that repeated the settings above are removed. The page also works in a browser that blocks the site's storage: the defaults apply, and a choice holds until the page is reloaded. The barcode search of the wine list shows its instruction under the field, where it fits on a phone. When Cellar cannot show a page at all, for instance with an unreadable database, the error page is in English and French and links back to the wine list, and an error in the admin keeps the admin's menu.

Colours now follow the theme you choose, in light and dark mode. Information boxes, dialog icons and the switch that shows the wine images take the theme's colour, while success and warning messages keep their green and amber; all of them stay readable in dark mode, and in light mode red is a little deeper, so that error messages stay readable on their tinted boxes. Notifications are now a plain card whose border and icon show their kind. A wine without an image shows a neutral placeholder instead of a purple block, the Statistics and Wine Shortage pages show their icons in the theme's colour and their figures in the text colour, and a wine's website link is underlined. The last drop-down lists drawn by the browser (the CSV delimiter, the backup mode, the filters of the backup and admin lists, the country or region of a new region or appellation, the label presets, the scanner's camera and the choice between bottles in bulk entry) now look like the other lists, and work from the keyboard, a typed letter included. Choosing Tab as the delimiter of a CSV import or export now really uses a tab: it used the two characters `\t` before.

Changes after 0.10.0.

For contributors: the database code moves from `src/lib/db/` to `src/lib/server/db/`, so that SvelteKit refuses to load it in the browser. Nothing changes when using Cellar.

Changing the status of bottles, or moving them, now uses the same dialog on the wine page, on the out-of-cellar page and in the bottles of a wine in the wine list, and the bulk barcode entry uses the same fields. The status list offers every status the bottles do not already have, and "Consumed" is proposed first, with today's date, which you can now clear to save a bottle consumed without a date. Confirm is disabled while the change is on its way, so a double click no longer adds a note twice, and a lost connection now shows a message instead of failing silently. When a bottle was deleted elsewhere, the message says that the list is already up to date instead of asking to reload it.

The barcode page now counts and exports only the codes generated with the current prefix, capitals included: for the prefix `CV`, `cv00000002`, `CVX0000001` and codes typed by hand in another format no longer count, and with an empty prefix, only the generated codes, made of digits, count instead of every barcode. The page also opens again with a prefix longer than 6 characters saved by an old version, and says to change it. In the bulk barcode entry, a code that differs from another only by its capitals now finds its own bottle instead of asking which one. A bottle created consumed or out of the cellar no longer takes the next automatic barcode, as in the CSV import: the bottle form lets you type one instead. When the session had expired, the bottle form shows the next barcode again once you log in. When the prefix has no number left, the form now lets you type a barcode, which the bottle keeps. The barcode settings now say that a prefix shares its numbers with the longer prefixes that add digits to it, as the empty prefix does with `123`. For scripts that call the API: with automatic barcodes on, `POST /api/bottles` now keeps a `barcode` given for a single bottle, without taking a number of the sequence, and refuses one given for several bottles (`422 barcode_for_one_bottle`), as it already did with automatic barcodes off; `GET /api/admin/next-barcode` answers `409 barcode_generation_off` while automatic barcodes are off, instead of `200` with an empty barcode; and a prefix longer than 6 characters, saved by an old version, now answers `409 barcode_prefix_too_long` instead of `500`.

Images: the wine form and the Images page of the admin now both take images of up to 20 MB; the admin stopped at 10 MB, and an image just under 20 MB was refused by the form. An image sent with a save of the wine form that failed is deleted when you close the form without saving. The Images page shows the wines that use each image, and its search finds images by the names of these wines too. Downloading images no longer builds the whole zip in memory first, and an image file that cannot be read gives an error message instead of stopping Cellar. The ZIP import of images copies only JPEG, PNG, WebP and GIF images, recognised by their content (BMP is no longer accepted; BMP images imported before still show), never lets a second file of the same name replace the first, and lists every other file in its report. A new image name must end in .jpg, .jpeg, .png, .gif or .webp and hold 255 bytes at most, and an image whose name holds a space, `#` or `?` now shows. For scripts, `docs/API.md` describes the changed answers of the image routes: image URLs are percent-encoded, and `GET /api/admin/images` gives the wines of each image.

Backups: a restore now keeps the automatic backup settings of your installation, so that a backup made in the cron mode no longer stops your automatic backups, and adds the upgrade actions of the backup's version to the Admin banner, marked "may already be done": tick those you have already taken. A wipe or a restore now deletes the image files that no wine uses any more (the backup made first keeps them), and a wipe holds the other saves until it ends, as a restore does. The backups that Cellar makes before a restore, a wipe or an import have their own label in the list. A backup larger than a restore accepts (2 GiB uncompressed, 10,000 files) is still made, with a warning. A backup name may now be longer than 50 characters, up to about 150, and a longer one gets a message instead of an error. After a restore, an import or a wipe, your browser downloads the backup of the previous data by itself, without making you wait. Cellar now removes at startup the temporary files that a stop during a restore, an import or a download of images left behind. Manual backups named "auto" before 0.6.0 are now listed as manual. For scripts: `GET /api/admin/list-backups` gives the types `safety-backup-restore`, `safety-backup-reset` and `safety-export-import`; `POST /api/admin/create-backup` and `create-export` answer `restorable`; `POST /api/admin/wipe-database` can answer `503 writes_held`, as the other writes can during a wipe; and `POST /api/admin/import-json` answers 500 instead of 422 when the server's disk fails.

For contributors: `pnpm test:e2e` runs four end-to-end journeys in Chromium (Playwright) against the built app, on a throwaway data folder: log in and add a wine with its bottles, consume a bottle and find it in the history, back up, wipe and restore the cellar, and put a bottle in a case. CI runs them in a job of their own. Nothing changes when using Cellar.

Adding a country, a region or an entry of the other lists now compares its name without capitals: adding "france" in the admin, or by a script, gives the existing "France" instead of a second entry, as the CSV import already did. The CSV import finds a region in the country, and an appellation in the region, that the file gives next to it, as the exports do, so two regions of the same name in two countries stay apart; a region or an appellation that is not under the country or the region given next to it is now reported as unknown instead of skipped. A row with more or fewer values than the header is reported alone instead of failing the whole file; a wine row already in the cellar but with an invalid value is reported as invalid instead of "already in the cellar"; and an invalid `imageName` is reported on that column. The results show the name of each table in your language, and a large file lists its first 1,000 skipped or failed rows instead of failing after the import. A new "Dry run" button shows the results without writing anything. A file named in capitals, such as `WINEBOTTLES.CSV`, is accepted; "Override all barcodes" is no longer preselected at the next import, and its help says that every row is then added, without looking for bottles already in the cellar. For scripts: each report of `POST /api/admin/import-csv` now gives the table (`table`, or `null`) and the file name (`file`) apart, instead of `<table> (<file>)` in `table`, lists at most 1,000 rows in `errors` and in `skipped` (the counts stay complete), and reports a row of another length with the problem `uneven_row`.

The history and out-of-cellar pages now sort like the other bottle tables, as 0.8.0 announced for the bottle details and the all-bottles dialog: names with an accent or a lowercase letter no longer sort after Z, and bottles without a value come last in both directions. Changing the history filter keeps the sort; on "All Wines", sorting by consumption date now really sorts by that date, with the bottles not consumed last, and "In Cave" no longer shows that column. Both pages have the same items-per-page menu, and Back, there and on a wine page, goes to the page you came from, or to the wine list when the page was opened in a new tab or from a link outside Cellar. Statistics: two regions of the same name in two countries, such as Central Valley, now have a bar each, with their country; Top 10 Producers shows 10 producers when there are that many, instead of 9 when some wines have none; an average with no price shows N/A instead of €0.00; and Recent Vintages shows a message instead of an empty frame when no vintage is less than 10 years old. The shortage page shows a purchase price of 0 instead of N/A, and lists wines with the same shortage by name. For scripts: `GET /api/statistics` gives each region of `winesByRegion` its `id` and `country`.

The admin pages now show the version of Cellar under their title. Docker: the image is about 60 MB smaller, it is built on an exact version of Node.js, and each image is started, and must report healthy, before it is published. Its healthcheck now gives Cellar 40 seconds to start and each check 10 seconds, the delays of `docker-compose.yml`, which no longer defines its own: if you copied `docker-compose.yml`, its healthcheck stays valid, and there is nothing to change. For contributors: CI fails when `src/lib/server/db/schema.ts` changes without its migration, and `pnpm install` now stops when its `prepare` script fails instead of ignoring the error.

Labels: the barcode page now measures the bars of a barcode as the PDF draws them, above the code value, and the bars fill that height instead of stopping at 30% of the label width, so the bars of wide labels print taller. Labels that show the code value are accepted as before, and those that hide it are accepted down to 10 mm of bars. The warning under 25 mm of bars now shows for more labels, such as the default layout of the barcode page and the Brother DK-11201, Dymo 30252 and Dymo 99010 presets, whose bars were already that short in the PDF. A start number or a range of codes past the last number that the prefix allows, such as 99,999 with the prefix `ABCDEF`, an invalid prefix typed in manual mode, or a prefix longer than 6 characters saved by an old version, now greys the PDF and CSV buttons and says why, and the preview of the range says "out of range" once. Next to the buttons of the label presets, the page now lists the errors that grey them. The Avery 8160 preset is now described as an inkjet sheet, not a laser one: the upgrade corrects it unless you changed its description. A copy of `label_presets.csv` in your `csv-imports` folder that differs from the one Cellar shipped only by its CRLF line endings, as Windows or another app often saves it, is now replaced like an unedited copy, and so is the copy of 0.9.0 and 0.10.0. Scanner: when the camera stops during a scan, for example because it was unplugged, the scanner says so and offers "Try again"; a browser that gives no access to the camera is no longer told to open Cellar over HTTPS. For scripts that call the API: `POST /api/barcode/pdf-labels` measures the bars of a barcode under the code value, so the `values` of `height_below_minimum` give the height of the bars, with a limit of 10 mm.

Container names are now unique, and so are the case names of a container: a name already taken, or two cases with the same name, is refused, with the reason under the field concerned (the API answers `409` with `duplicate_container` or `duplicate_case`). Upgrading renames the duplicates that earlier versions allowed rather than merging them, and no bottle moves: the second container "A" becomes "A (2)" and its case "A1" becomes "A (2)1", and a second case "A1" in a container becomes "A1 (2)". Rename them as you like afterwards. A JSON export made by an earlier version with such duplicates cannot be imported: restore a backup zip instead: the restore repairs the duplicates. A space typed before a case name is now kept: in container "Fridge", the case " top" is named "Fridge top". The CSV export of the bottles has a new `containerName` column, which the CSV import uses to put each bottle back in its case even when two containers have cases of the same name, and a case imported into a container that already has cases now goes after them. Deleting a container or a label preset now asks in Cellar's own confirmation, which closes when you leave the page. A container without cases shows a button to add one, a large case draws 24 places and then the number of the others, and a container named, for example, "Wine Column X" keeps its name when saved. For scripts: `PUT /api/storage-containers/{id}` takes an optional `updatedAt` and answers `409 container_changed` when the container changed since then, and `GET /api/storage-containers` lists the containers in the order of the storage page.

The wine list keeps its search, filters and sort in the page address: coming back from a wine finds them as you left them, and a link to the list shares them. It filters once typing pauses instead of at each key, its region and country filters tell apart two regions of the same name in two countries, and its barcode search finds first the code exactly as typed, then the same code in other capitals, then the codes that contain it. The page is lighter, as it loads only the bottles you still own: the barcode search and the bulk barcode entry no longer find a consumed bottle. "Add Bottle" no longer offers the wine of a bottle you cancelled. For scripts that call the API: `GET /api/wines` still lists every bottle, consumed ones included, but now gives each wine as `{ "definition", "bottles" }`: the fields of its first bottle are no longer spread beside them, a wine without bottles no longer has the virtual id `def-<wine id>`, and the bottles no longer repeat the wine in `definition` (see the upgrade action).

The API answers more consistently, which scripts can rely on. A path under `/api` that matches no route answers `404` and a method that a route lacks `405`, in the API error format instead of a web page or plain text; every `422 invalid_body` lists the field at fault in `details`; a `PUT` returns what it saved, except `PUT /api/access-code`, which answers `204` as the code is a secret; the routes that the 0.7.0 notes listed answer `201` for a creation and `204` for a deletion; deleting a bottle through either route, or reading the locations of a wine, answers `404` for one that does not exist; a label preset that does not exist answers `404` before its body is checked; and `GET /api/admin/download-backup` names the backup by `filename`, as the other backup routes do (see the upgrade action for what changes for scripts).

A purchase price or a current value can no longer be negative: the bottle form says so under the field, and the API refuses it. A CSV or JSON import still imports a bottle that has one, without that price or value, and writes it into the bottle's notes; the upgrade does the same for the bottles already in your cellar. Notes are still cut at 5,000 characters, so a note that was already that long cannot take the line.

The session timeout setting now says that a change applies to the next logins, and that changing the access code ends the other sessions at once. In the storage page, a container whose cases were imported with their own names, such as "Top1" and "Bottom1", can be saved again: each case keeps its own name after the container's ("FridgeTop1" and "FridgeBottom1" in container "Fridge") instead of both becoming "1", which was refused. Saving such a container renames its cases this way.

Texts: English now says "wine" where it said "wine definition" ("Add wine", "Edit wine", "Wines" in the statistics and the admin), as French already did, and both languages drop the word from their other messages. French uses one typography (’, « », …), calls a storage case « case » everywhere, and its search fields read as sentences (« Rechercher des pays… »). A file that is not valid CSV says how to fix its quotes, and a JSON export refused for one of its rows says what is wrong with the row in your language; for scripts, the `422 invalid_export` answer of such a row adds `details.problems`, with problem codes like those of the CSV import. An expired session during an action of the Images or Backups pages of the admin, or of the label presets, now only opens the login dialog, without an error beside it. Dates such as a purchase date no longer show the day before in a browser west of UTC, and the Images page of the admin now shows the time each image changed, next to its date. An upgrade action that you tick stays in the banner until your next visit, so that a wrong tick can be undone. For contributors: a text shared by several pages has one i18n key, in `common.*`; the `ui.*` keys moved to the namespace of their page; `pnpm i18n:check` has tests, and also fails on the text of `alert`, `confirm` and `prompt`, on the same text under two keys, and on French typography.
actions: Only if your own scripts call the Cellar API: send `GET /api/admin/download-backup?filename=` instead of `?file=`, which now answers `422`. Read what a `PUT` saved instead of `{ success: true }` from `PUT /api/settings`, `/api/admin/backup-settings`, `/api/admin/barcode-settings` (with its `conflictInfo`), `/api/admin/upgrade-actions` and `/api/admin/images` (the image as `GET /api/admin/images` lists it, its wines in `wines`), and expect `204` without a body from `PUT /api/access-code`. Read the name of the backup made before a wipe in `backup` of `POST /api/admin/wipe-database`, instead of `backups.database` (its `size` is gone). Expect `204` without a body from `DELETE /api/admin/wine-definitions/{id}` and `DELETE /api/admin/images`, and `201` from `POST /api/admin/upload-image` and `POST /api/admin/import-images-zip`. No longer expect `message` from `POST /api/bottles` nor `success` from `POST /api/upload/image`. Send a purchase price and a current value of 0 or more to `POST` and `PATCH /api/bottles`, which answer `422` to a negative one. Expect `404` from `DELETE /api/admin/wine-bottles/{id}` for a bottle that does not exist, and from `GET /api/wines/{id}/locations` for a wine that does not exist. Read the wine of `GET /api/bottles/non-consumed` in `definition` instead of `wineDefinition`, and the location of `GET /api/definitions/{id}` in `appellation` only, as `appellations`, `regions` and `countries` are gone. Handle `409 barcode_generation_off` from `GET /api/admin/next-barcode` while automatic barcodes are off, instead of `200` with an empty `barcode`. Read each wine of `GET /api/wines` as `{ "definition", "bottles" }`, as the fields of its first bottle are no longer at the top level, a wine without bottles no longer has the id `def-<wine id>`, and each bottle no longer repeats its wine in `definition`. `docs/API.md` describes every answer.

summary:
Follow-ups to the fixes of 0.9.0.

The CSV import now adds every wine of a wines file that differs from another only in another column, such as its rating, description or image, instead of the first one only. Their bottles are reported as matching several wines even when you import the bottles file after the wines file, instead of being added to the first wine. The same row given twice still adds one wine, and importing a wines file again into a cellar that already holds its wines adds nothing, even if you edited these wines since. For the same reason, if an earlier version imported only the first of such wines, importing the file again does not add the others: add them in the app and move their bottles, or import the files into an empty cellar.

A note typed when consuming bottles, on the out-of-cellar page, on a wine's page, or in the bottle details or Bulk entry dialogs of the wine list, is now added on a new line after the notes of each bottle, instead of replacing them; a bottle without notes gets the note alone. A line under the note field now says so. For scripts that call the API: `PATCH /api/bottles` takes an optional `addedNote` beside `ids` and `changes` for this; `notes` in `changes` still replaces the notes.

Bottle notes and wine descriptions now hold at most 5,000 characters, instead of 100,000. The forms count the characters as you type and stop at the limit. The upgrade cuts every longer note or description to its first 5,000 characters: the rest of the text is deleted. To keep such texts whole, make a backup before upgrading, and export your cellar as CSV files in Admin: the CSV files open in a spreadsheet, where you can copy the longer texts. Restoring a backup of an earlier version, or importing an export or a CSV file of an earlier version, cuts them the same way. An emoji counts as two characters or more in the forms, so a note or a description close to the limit that holds emoji may need a few characters removed before it is saved again. A note typed when consuming bottles that would make the notes of some bottles longer than 5,000 characters is refused with a message, and no bottle is changed: shorten the note, or the notes of these bottles. For scripts that call the API: a longer `notes` or `description` answers `422`, and so does `PATCH /api/bottles` (`notes_too_long`) when its `addedNote` does not fit after the notes of a bottle; line breaks sent as CRLF in `notes`, `description` or `addedNote` are stored as LF.

Fixes from the pre-1.0 audit.

If you build Cellar from a Git checkout of `develop`, the build now carries the number of the next release candidate, such as 0.9.0-rc.0, instead of that of the last release. Starting an earlier release, such as 0.8.0, on a database that such a build has used is refused, as for any older version, because that release does not know the changes that build made to the database. Such a build counts as a release candidate: upgrade actions added to its version later are not shown in the admin page, so read the actions in the release notes of each version you install.

On the out-of-cellar page, on a wine's page and in the bottle details of the wine list, a note typed under Consumed and then hidden by picking another status no longer replaces the notes of the bottles.

The CSV export of bottles has a new `typeName` column, so wines that differ only by their type keep their own bottles through an export and an import; bottles that an import cannot match to a single wine, such as those of wines that differ only by another column like the rating or description (imported with their wines file, which adds the first of these wines only), or those of wines that differ only by their type in a bottles file exported by an earlier version, are now reported instead of being added to the first wine.

The number fields of wines and bottles, such as prices, vintages, ratings and quantities, and the label measurements and case capacities now read "12,5" and "12.5" alike, whatever the language of your browser: an English browser no longer saves "12,5" as 125, and a value that is not a number, such as "1e", is refused with a message instead of erasing the field or saving a default. In the wine, bottle and storage forms, the message under the field says which number it expects, such as "Enter a whole number between 0 and 9,999". The fields show numbers in the language of the interface, with a decimal comma in French. The storage page no longer gives 5 bottles to a case whose capacity was left empty: it asks for a whole number of bottles between 1 and 1,000.

The label presets that Cellar ships are fixed: the Avery sheets (5160, 5161, 5162, 5163, 5164 and 8160) now follow Avery's templates, so a 5160 sheet prints all 30 of its labels on the die cuts, instead of 27 drifting off them, and Brother DK-22210, Dymo 30320, Zebra 2x1, Generic 40x25 and Generic 50x30, too narrow for a barcode, print a QR code. The upgrade corrects these presets unless you renamed them or changed their measurements: compare such an Avery preset with the template of its sheet, and switch such a narrow preset to a QR code. It also replaces `label_presets.csv` in your `csv-imports` folder unless you edited it: if you did, rename it and restart Cellar, which writes the corrected file, then carry your changes over to it. A preset whose labels cannot be printed, such as a QR code under 10 mm or labels larger than the page, can no longer be saved. The barcode page now opens on labels that print (56 mm wide instead of 50), lists the warnings apart from the errors that prevent printing and saving a preset, and says under each label field which number it expects.

A backup of the list in the admin page is restored, or imported, where it is on the server, instead of going through the browser: a backup of more than 500 MB that Cellar made can now be restored. Restoring or importing a file chosen on your computer no longer takes about five times its size in memory. For scripts, `POST /api/admin/restore` and `POST /api/admin/import-json` no longer take a form: send the name of a backup or export of the list as JSON, `{ "filename": "cellar-backup-….zip" }`, as `DELETE /api/admin/delete-backup` takes it, or a zip as the raw body with `Content-Type: application/zip` (500 MB at most). A form is refused with 400.

For scripts that call the API: `PUT /api/bottles/{id}` is removed and answers 405; use `PATCH /api/bottles/{id}`, which changes only the fields it is given. The API is now documented in `docs/API.md`, linked from README-Docker: each route with the session it needs, its body, its answer and its errors, and how a script logs in.

Bottles saved with a vintage of 0, as the CSV import of 0.6.0 and earlier did for a blank vintage, now have no vintage: they no longer show "0" on the wine cards, in the statistics, the history, the admin pages, the CSV export or the labels, no longer come first when sorting by "Oldest vintage", and the "Without vintage" filter still finds them. A vintage of 0 entered in a form, sent to the API or read from a CSV file is saved as no vintage.
actions: Scripts that call `PUT /api/bottles/{id}` must switch to `PATCH` and send only the fields to change.

summary:
Frontend foundations.

About 1,300 lines of unused front-end code are removed, and `pnpm knip` lists unused files, exports and dependencies.

Wine type and colour badges have a colour for the types and colours you create yourself, instead of grey. In the statistics, the type pie uses the colours of the type badges instead of shades of grey, rosé wines are no longer grey in the colour pie, and yellow wines no longer share the colour of white wines. The code that reads the API is fully typed.

Pages show their data as soon as they load, without a loading spinner: the server renders the wine list, a wine, the shortage, statistics, storage, barcode, history and out-of-cellar pages. History and out-of-cellar are filtered, sorted and paged on the server, with their state in the URL, so a filtered page can be bookmarked or reloaded; the out-of-cellar selection is kept from one page to the next. An unknown page or wine shows a translated error page.

Dates, prices and file sizes follow the interface language everywhere, and the consumption date suggested just after midnight is today, not yesterday. Bottle tables share one look, with headers you can sort from the keyboard; one pagination, with page numbers, is used across the app, the admin included. In the bottle details of the wine list and in the all-bottles dialog of the storage page, names with an accent or a lowercase letter no longer sort after Z. Bottle statuses are translated everywhere, and a half-point rating rounds to the nearest star. The wine list's vintage and origin filters only consider the bottles you still own.

On the storage page, cases are identified by id and kept in their own order (a migration keeps the order shown until now), so a container `A1` with case `1` and a container `A` with case `11` are no longer mixed up, and cases whose name does not end with a number are shown. Editing a container is a draft: nothing is saved until you click Update, cancelling changes nothing, and removing a case that still holds bottles is refused with a message naming the case. The occupancy is counted the same way everywhere, and the all-bottles dialog refreshes the page after a change.

The barcode page has one label form in both barcode modes, checked as you type by the same code the server runs, and its remaining English texts are translated. Label presets save the border option, a saved preset stays selected, QR code PDFs are about 8 times smaller, and the barcode dialog of a bottle draws its code itself. For scripts that call the API: `POST /api/barcode/pdf-labels` refuses QR codes smaller than 10 mm (422 `label_too_small`), and that error lists `details.issues` instead of `details.warnings` and `details.recommendations`.

The wine list, the wine page, the shortage and statistics pages and their dialogs use Svelte 5 throughout. The dark theme applies at once to the status dialog of a wine page, and the placeholder icon of a wine without an image is drawn in full.

The admin is split into pages, Settings, Backups, Data and Images, each with its own address and loaded on the server (`/admin` opens Settings). Its busy indicators work, errors from a proxy or a lost connection are shown, restoring a backup from the list is labelled correctly, and the backup taken before a restore or an import is announced only once it has been downloaded.

The wine and bottle forms are rewritten: they check each field with the same rules as the server and show what is wrong under the field itself, including a used-up barcode prefix as soon as the form opens, a duplicate barcode or a full case. They fit phone screens, a new wine's image shows at once, the search among existing images works again, storage cases are listed in the order of the storage page, and a date being typed is no longer erased.

Cellar picks its language from a cookie, then from the browser's language, and pages arrive from the server already in that language; changing the language reloads the page. The language chosen with an earlier version is not kept: choose it again in the preferences if needed. Every text goes through the language files, with correct plurals; the French interface is reviewed (sentence case, « code-barres »), and the CSV import guide and its per-row messages are translated.

Accessibility: the login dialog keeps the keyboard focus and closes with Escape, icon-only buttons have a name, the navigation moves into a menu on narrow screens and no longer makes pages scroll sideways, the dark theme no longer flashes white on load, and checkboxes and field examples are easier to see. A refused write opens the login dialog instead of a toast. For scripts that call the API: `POST /api/admin/import-csv` now lists, for each refused row, `problems` (codes) instead of `error` (a text), and for each skipped row a `reason` object with a `code`.
actions: Only if your own scripts call the Cellar API: `PUT /api/storage-containers/{id}` must list every case of the container, in order, as a case left out is now deleted.

summary:
API foundations: every request is validated, errors follow one format, and the business rules live in the server.

The server checks every request before it writes anything: a request it cannot accept gets a clear answer instead of a server error, and the app shows the reason, translated, where it used to show a generic message or nothing. Errors follow one format, `{ error: { code, message, details } }`, with 201 for a creation, 204 for a deletion, 404, 409, 413 and 422. JSON bodies are limited to 1 MB. Wines and bottles refer to their type, color, classification, format and origin by id only: a typo no longer adds an entry to these lists, and new origins are created from the bottle form. A manual barcode given to several bottles at once is refused instead of dropped.

The business rules live in the server, in one service per domain. A storage case can no longer hold more bottles in the cellar than its capacity: adding, moving or bringing back bottles into a full case, and lowering a capacity below the bottles of its case, are refused with a clear message. A case already over its capacity, after an import or with an older version, can still be edited and emptied. The capacity of a case and the locations of a wine count the bottles in the cellar only, as the storage page does. Settings, sessions, the access code and label presets are saved all or nothing, and other changes wait a few seconds while a JSON export is imported, as they do during a restore. A backup downloads as a stream instead of being loaded in memory, and the barcode CSV exports escape quotes.

The CSV import is rewritten. It reads each file once and imports them all in one transaction, about five times faster: 2,000 bottles take a quarter of a second. A row the database refuses cancels the whole import and names its file and row; incomplete rows are still skipped and reported, and a `dryRun` field returns the report without writing anything. It keeps only the known columns of each table and never takes ids, and a row that names a missing reference is reported instead of being imported without it. Bottles name their wine by producer, appellation, classification and color, which the bottle export now writes too, and a wine the file cannot tell apart is reported: the bottles of homonymous wines in an export from 0.6.0 or older are reported rather than imported, so export again from this version first. Importing the same file or its export again adds nothing, except the bottles in the cellar that had no barcode and got one at the first import: import the export taken after it instead. Automatic barcodes go to bottles in the cellar only, consumed bottles keep the barcode of the file, a blank vintage stays blank and ratings keep their decimals. Both imports repair older statuses, ratings, grape varieties and target quantities with a note, as the 0.6.0 upgrade does, and answer in the API error format. The import no longer floods the container logs: set `DEBUG=csv-import` to see its log.

Changing the status or the place of several bottles is now one request that changes all of them or none, instead of one request per bottle: it replaces the count of partial successes added in 0.4.0, and a bottle deleted elsewhere is dropped from the selection. Editing a bottle saves only the fields you changed, so it no longer resets the time of its dates or overwrites a change made meanwhile. For scripts, `PATCH /api/bottles/{id}` changes only the fields it is given and `PATCH /api/bottles` takes `{ ids, changes }`; `PUT /api/bottles/{id}` still works.

The eight reference lists (wine types, colors, formats and classifications, origins, countries, regions and appellations) are served by one set of routes, `/api/<table>`, for the forms and the admin page alike. Editing an entry returns it, editing or deleting one that does not exist answers 404, and deleting one still in use is refused with the number of rows that use it, even when a change comes in between. Adding a name that already exists returns the existing entry, and the admin page says so. Lists are sorted by name.

Unused and duplicate endpoints are removed: `POST /api/wines` and `GET` or `PUT /api/wines/{id}` (use `/api/definitions`), `GET /api/admin/auto-backup` (use `GET /api/admin/backup-settings`), and `POST /api/admin/restore-label-presets`, `seed-manufacturer-presets` and `cleanup-csv`. Admin answers give backups and exports by file name instead of revealing where the server keeps its data. The CSV export of the admin page no longer writes files on the server, and an export of every table now saves all its files, wines and bottles included. CSV exports put a `'` before a cell that a spreadsheet would run as a formula, and the CSV import removes it.

Upgrading from a version before 0.2.0 now removes the old access code from the database file as soon as Cellar starts: since 0.6.0 it could remain there, in clear, until the database was next closed. After a restore or a JSON import, the browser downloads the backup that Cellar makes of the current data first, as the message says: since 0.4.0 at least, it was only kept on the server.
actions: Only if your own scripts call the Cellar API: read an error from `error.code` and `error.message`, as errors are no longer a plain `error` text; send ids, not names, for the type, color, classification, format and origin of wines and bottles; call `/api/<table>` instead of `/api/admin/<table>` for wine types, colors, formats and classifications, origins, countries, regions and appellations, and send `name` for wine types and colors; read the saved entry from a PUT instead of `{ success: true }`; and use `/api/definitions` instead of `/api/wines` to create or change a wine.

summary:
Data foundations: one database connection, migrations at startup, transactions, constraints, reliable backups and restores, and an upgrade check at startup.

Cellar opens a single connection to its database, in WAL mode. The data folders and the database file can be moved with the environment variables `DATA_DIR`, `DATABASE_PATH`, `UPLOADS_DIR` and `CSV_IMPORTS_DIR`; their defaults are the paths used so far, so nothing changes for existing installations. While Cellar runs, `cellar.db-wal` and `cellar.db-shm` sit next to `cellar.db`: copy the data folder only while Cellar is stopped, or use a backup made from the admin page, and keep it on a local disk, as WAL mode does not suit network shares (NFS, SMB).

Database migrations run when the server starts, before it accepts requests: a failed migration stops Cellar with a clear message in the container logs instead of serving a half-updated database, and the first page no longer waits for them. A broken file in `csv-imports` is named in the logs, and the other files are still imported.

Operations that write several rows are all or nothing: importing a JSON export or CSV files, wiping the database, creating several bottles, deleting a storage container and restoring the default label presets either complete or leave your data unchanged. Importing an automatic export made by an older version, which lacked several tables and could empty the cellar, is refused; automatic exports now hold every table. In a CSV import, incomplete rows are still skipped and reported, but a row the database refuses cancels the whole import. Deleting a case, container or wine that still holds bottles is refused with a clear message.

The database enforces its rules: a barcode belongs to one bottle only, region and appellation names are unique within their country or region, statuses and ratings (1 to 5) are checked, and every link between tables is indexed. The upgrade repairs existing data that breaks these rules: duplicate regions and appellations are merged, a barcode shared by several bottles stays on one of them, unknown statuses become "out of cellar" and out-of-range ratings are removed; each such change is written, in English, in the bottle's notes or the wine's description. Deleting a case or container that only holds bottles that left the cellar is now allowed: those bottles lose their location. A JSON export from an older version that holds such rows is refused with an explanation: restore a backup zip instead, which is repaired when restored.

The default CSV files live in one place in the image. `wine_bottle_formats.csv` in your `csv-imports` folder is no longer read, as it duplicated `wine_formats.csv`: if you added lines to it, move them to `wine_formats.csv`. Hand-made header lines in `appellations.csv` and files saved as "CSV UTF-8" by Excel are read correctly.

Backups are reliable. Each one holds a consistent snapshot of the database, even while Cellar is being used, and a backup interrupted by a stop never looks complete. A restore first checks the file: only a Cellar backup is accepted and only its images are copied. It keeps your access code and your session, and other changes wait a few seconds while it runs. Backups from every version since 0.1.0 restore without restarting Cellar. A new automatic backup frequency applies at once, and automatic backups and automatic exports are each kept up to the chosen number. The External Cron Job mode is back: in the automatic backup settings, Cellar generates a token and shows the command to give your cron job (see [Automatic backups](https://github.com/Lulu300/cellar/blob/main/README-Docker.md#automatic-backups)). The archive library moves to archiver 8.

Cellar checks the upgrade path when it starts. It records its version, lists the upgrade actions still to take in the container logs and in a banner on the admin page, where you can tick them, and warns when `ORIGIN` is missing. It refuses to start, changing nothing, on a database last used by a newer version, or when the upgrade skips a version that must be installed first. Versions before 0.6.0 did not record themselves: the first start of 0.6.0 judges the previous version from the database and marks the older actions as "may already be done". A restore applies the same checks to the backup. Earlier versions do not have this check: to go back to one of them, restore a backup made before the upgrade rather than starting the older image on the upgraded data.

Barcode numbering uses a counter per prefix stored in the database: two bottles never get the same code, and the number of a deleted bottle is never given again, even after a wipe or after restoring an older backup.

Upgrade of the foundations before the larger refactorings.

Cellar now runs on SvelteKit 3, Vite 8 and TypeScript 6, the base the next refactorings build on. Nothing changes for Docker users: the image keeps reading `ORIGIN` from the same `.env` file and still refuses writes sent from other web pages. Those who run Cellar from source, or who override the container's start command, must start it with `node server.js`: see the upgrade action.

The barcode scanner was rewritten on the standard BarcodeDetector API, with a decoder served by Cellar itself when the browser has none (Firefox, iPhone): labels are now read on a dark background or with the preview border, where the old scanner often failed, and the scanner still reads the retail codes bottles may carry (EAN, UPC, Code 39, Data Matrix). It works without Internet access. The preview border of PDF labels no longer crosses the barcode.

Server libraries: better-sqlite3 moves to version 13 (SQLite 3.53), which ships ready-made binaries, so building the image no longer compiles it; building it yourself now works on amd64 and arm64 only, the two platforms the published images cover. New identifiers and uploaded image names are random UUIDs; existing ones keep working.

The Docker guide (README-Docker.md) was checked against the code: it explains how to install and update Cellar from a release archive while the repository and its image are private, what the `csv-imports` folder is for (your own CSV files are imported from the browser), that the scanner camera needs HTTPS or `localhost`, and how to back up and restore safely.
actions: Only if you run Cellar from source instead of Docker, or if your container overrides the image's start command (for example `command: node build` in a compose file or a NAS template): start the built app with `node server.js` instead of `node build`, with `ORIGIN` set as before, for example `ORIGIN=http://localhost:3000 node server.js`. SvelteKit 3 no longer reads `ORIGIN` in `node build`, so every save, import, upload or delete would fail with 403. Other Docker users have nothing to do: the image starts this way and keeps reading `ORIGIN` from the same `.env` file.

summary:
Bug fixes visible in everyday use.

Barcodes and labels: every code has the 10 characters the bottles carry, so the barcode CSV export, the PDF labels and the next-code preview agree. A used-up prefix is reported instead of producing truncated codes, and longer manual codes such as EAN-13 no longer shift the numbering. The numbering continues after the 13-character codes generated before September 2025, for example in an old backup, instead of restarting at 1 and reusing numbers already printed on labels. PDF labels draw their barcodes as vectors, from a corrected Code 128 encoder, with the blank margins scanners need: they scan reliably and the files are about a hundred times smaller. Invalid label options are refused with a clear message instead of producing a broken PDF. The barcode scanner turns the camera off when its dialog closes. Labels printed before 0.4.0 may have to be printed again: see the upgrade action.

Wines and bottles: the wine list can be sorted by name, producer, oldest vintage, average price, rating or bottle count, computed over the bottles you still own, and each wine shows its range of vintages. The wine form no longer clears or reverts what you typed when you choose a region, and a slow answer for another wine no longer fills it. In the cellar history, changing the filter or the page size goes back to the first page instead of showing an empty list. The out-of-cellar list shows where each bottle was stored, sorts by wine, and reports how many bottles were updated when only some of them could be. The statistics pie charts are drawn when there is only one category.

Administration and data: deleting images works again and asks for confirmation when wines still use them. "Select all", "Export" and the selection follow the image search: an image hidden by the search, or by renaming it, is no longer selected, so "Delete selection" only deletes what you see. Editing a bottle format shows its current name. Backups and exports whose name contains characters such as œ, € or an emoji can be downloaded and restored again, and keep their real name in the browser. A cellar exported to CSV can be imported again without duplicating its wines, and a CSV export with a custom name can be downloaded. The country "Pays", the region "Région" and the appellation "Appellation", which every installation got from the header line of the appellations file, are removed when nothing uses them.

Also: the README presents Cellar and links to the Docker installation and the upgrade guide, csv-parse was updated to fix a vulnerability, and the Preferences page shows the application version.
actions: Only if you printed barcode labels before 0.4.0. Labels made from the barcode **CSV export** carry 13-character codes that match no bottle: print them again. Labels from the **PDF** do not scan on many label templates, because their barcode was cut off at its right end: scan one label from each PDF sheet you printed, and print again every sheet whose labels do not scan. Print the new labels from the PDF or from a new CSV export. The codes stored on your bottles do not change, so a reprinted label matches the same bottle.

summary: Safety nets before the refactoring. Every change now goes through automated tests, linting and formatting, a translation check and a CI that must pass before a Docker image is published. Dependencies were cleaned up: unused packages are gone, pnpm is the only package manager, and the front-end and server libraries got their minor updates, which fixes the known vulnerabilities in svelte, yauzl and source-map-js. The Docker image is about 10% smaller. Interface texts that showed a raw translation key now show the right text, and a few icons look slightly different after the icon library update.
actions: Only if you run Cellar from source instead of Docker: use Node 24 and pnpm 10. `pnpm install` now refuses other Node versions, and runs the exact pnpm version set by `packageManager` in `package.json`. `package-lock.json` is gone, so `npm install` is no longer supported. Docker users have nothing to do.

summary:
First release of the security clean-up. The server now checks who may change things: browsing the cellar stays open, but every save, import, upload or delete, and the whole admin area, need a login session held by the server, and editing the browser's storage no longer grants anything. The access code is stored hashed, there is no default `1234` any more (the first code is chosen with a one-time setup token printed in the server logs), and wrong codes are limited per client. Cellar is meant for a home network or a VPN, not for direct exposure to the Internet. The server also rejects writes sent from other web pages (CSRF origin check), so it must know the URL you open it with. Website links and storage names can no longer inject scripts, and names sent to the server (backups, CSV exports, imported images, barcode prefixes) can no longer reach files outside their folder; barcode prefixes are limited to 6 letters, digits or hyphens. Uploaded zips are checked before extraction, so a malformed or oversized archive is refused instead of crashing the server. Uploaded images are identified from their content: only JPEG, PNG, WebP and GIF are accepted, and images whose name starts with a dot are no longer served. The Docker image runs as an unprivileged user, is about 40% smaller, caps request bodies at 512 MB instead of 10 GB, stops at once on `docker stop`, and refuses to start, with a message explaining the fix, when it cannot write to its data folders. A crash that could stop the server while it served an image is fixed. The external cron mode for automatic backups is unavailable until it gets a token. Vulnerable dependencies were upgraded, and Docker images are now published only for tagged releases, with release notes and an upgrade guide.

Read every upgrade action below before upgrading. If you installed 0.2.0-rc.1, the actions about data ownership, cron backups, the access code, reverse proxies and old backups were added after it and apply to you as well. Since 0.2.0-rc.2, the data ownership command uses the public `alpine` image, and choosing a new access code needs the setup token from the logs.
actions: Set `ORIGIN` to the exact URL you open Cellar with: scheme, host and port, no trailing slash (for example `ORIGIN=http://192.168.1.20:3005`). With the repository's `docker-compose.yml`, take the new version of the file, copy `.env.example` to `.env` next to it and fill in `ORIGIN`: `docker compose` refuses to start without it. With your own compose file or `docker run`, add the variable to the container's environment. If `ORIGIN` is missing or does not match the URL in the browser, pages load but every save, import, upload or delete fails with 403. Behind a reverse proxy that serves several hostnames, set `PROTOCOL_HEADER` and `HOST_HEADER` instead: see [Application URL (ORIGIN)](https://github.com/Lulu300/cellar/blob/main/README-Docker.md#application-url-origin).

Cellar now runs as an unprivileged user (uid 1000) instead of root, so the data written by earlier versions, which belongs to root, must be given to that user before you start the new version. With the repository's `docker-compose.yml`, run `sudo chown -R 1000:1000 docker-data` next to it. With any other setup (other folders, named volumes, or no `sudo` on the host), run this command with the folders or volumes your container mounts as `-v` sources, and drop the `-v` of any you do not mount: `docker run --rm -v <data>:/app/data -v <uploads>:/app/static/uploads -v <csv-imports>:/app/csv-imports alpine chown -R 1000:1000 /app/data /app/static/uploads /app/csv-imports`. To run Cellar as another account instead, for example the one that owns your NAS shares (find its numbers with `id <account>`, often `1026:100` on Synology or `99:100` on Unraid), add `user: "1026:100"` to the service and use `1026:100` in place of `1000:1000` in these commands. If you skip this step, the container stops right after starting, and its log names the folders and files it cannot write to and how to fix them: see [Data ownership](https://github.com/Lulu300/cellar/blob/main/README-Docker.md#data-ownership).

If automatic backups use the **External Cron Job** mode, the cron job that runs `curl -X POST …/api/admin/auto-backup` now fails and no backup is made: the admin API requires a login session. In Cellar, open Admin, then the automatic backup settings, and set **Backup Mode** to **Internal Scheduler**; on a version before 0.6.0, restart the container afterwards, as saving the settings did not start the scheduler yet. From 0.6.0 on, you can instead keep the External Cron Job mode, with a token that Cellar generates: see [Automatic backups](https://github.com/Lulu300/cellar/blob/main/README-Docker.md#automatic-backups).

If your access code was still the default `1234`, it is removed when Cellar starts. To choose a new one, open Cellar and enter the setup token that the server prints in the container logs (`docker compose logs cellar`). A code you had chosen keeps working. See [Access code](https://github.com/Lulu300/cellar/blob/main/README-Docker.md#access-code).

Behind a reverse proxy, set `ADDRESS_HEADER` (and `XFF_DEPTH`) so that wrong access codes are counted per client: otherwise every request seems to come from the proxy, and one client's wrong codes block everyone. See [Client addresses behind a reverse proxy](https://github.com/Lulu300/cellar/blob/main/README-Docker.md#client-addresses-behind-a-reverse-proxy).
Backups made before 0.2.0 hold the access code in clear. Delete the copies you no longer need, or change the code if copies are kept elsewhere.

summary: First tagged version: the application as it was on `main` at 556c7bb (2026-10-08). Earlier changes are only recorded in the git history.
